_about: Hand-written. The guideline text the vibes check may quote. 'quoted' entries are copied word for word from the City of Toronto Official Plan, Chapter 4 (checked on toronto.ca, November 18, 2026). 'summary' entries are this project's plain-words summaries of City pages, NOT official wording: the app labels them as summaries. Check the links before relying on any of it. The vibes check gives opinions for discussion only and never changes a PASS or FAIL.

guidelines.name: Official Plan 4.1.5 (b): lots
guidelines.text: Development in established Neighbourhoods will respect and reinforce the existing physical character of each geographic neighbourhood, including in particular: prevailing size and configuration of lots;

guidelines.name: Official Plan 4.1.5 (c): height, massing and scale
guidelines.text: Development in established Neighbourhoods will respect and reinforce the existing physical character of each geographic neighbourhood, including in particular: prevailing heights, massing, scale, density and dwelling type of nearby residential properties;

guidelines.name: Official Plan 4.1.5 (d): building types
guidelines.text: Development in established Neighbourhoods will respect and reinforce the existing physical character of each geographic neighbourhood, including in particular: prevailing building type(s);

guidelines.name: Official Plan 4.1.5 (e): driveways and garages
guidelines.text: Development in established Neighbourhoods will respect and reinforce the existing physical character of each geographic neighbourhood, including in particular: prevailing location, design and elevations relative to the grade of driveways and garages;

guidelines.name: Official Plan 4.1.5 (f): front setbacks
guidelines.text: Development in established Neighbourhoods will respect and reinforce the existing physical character of each geographic neighbourhood, including in particular: prevailing setbacks of buildings from the street or streets;

guidelines.name: Official Plan 4.1.5 (g): rear and side yards
guidelines.text: Development in established Neighbourhoods will respect and reinforce the existing physical character of each geographic neighbourhood, including in particular: prevailing patterns of rear and side yard setbacks and landscaped open space;

guidelines.name: Official Plan 4.1.5 (h): special features
guidelines.text: Development in established Neighbourhoods will respect and reinforce the existing physical character of each geographic neighbourhood, including in particular: continuation of special landscape or built-form features that contribute to the unique physical character

guidelines.name: Official Plan 4.1.5 (i): heritage
guidelines.text: Development in established Neighbourhoods will respect and reinforce the existing physical character of each geographic neighbourhood, including in particular: conservation of heritage buildings, structures and landscapes.

guidelines.name: Official Plan 4.1.9 (c): privacy and sunlight (infill)
guidelines.text: provide adequate privacy, sunlight and sky views for occupants of new and existing buildings by ensuring adequate distance and separation between building walls

guidelines.name: Garden suites: City summary of rules (paraphrased)
guidelines.text: Garden suites are allowed in rear yards that don't back onto a public lane. Angular planes limit their height and mass so they step down toward neighbours. Trees are protected, and the lot can't be split off (severed) from the main house.

guidelines.name: Laneway suites: City page (paraphrased)
guidelines.text: Laneway suites are for lots that back onto a public lane. Zoning limits their height, size and separation from the main house, and requires soft landscaping between the suite and the house.

guidelines.name: Heritage Conservation District plan (paraphrased)
guidelines.text: In a Heritage Conservation District, changes that can be seen from the street are reviewed against that district's plan, which describes the district's heritage character (materials, rooflines, porches, windows). Read the plan for your district before designing.
